title: Sampled Stream Adapters — UX-first PRD (draft)
content:
TL;DR: Propose a lightweight ‘sampled stream adapter’ layer that lets clients receive periodic, multi‑fidelity updates from streaming model output. The adapter gives SDKs an explicit primitive for sampling intermediate hypotheses, attaching structured deltas, and coordinating tool calls (including suspend/resume) without requiring full transcript checkpoints on every token. A UX-first surface that reduces client bandwidth, improves perceived latency, and makes tool-handshake semantics explicit for mobile and constrained clients.

Context / problem we keep seeing
- Apps want partial, useful signals quickly (progress, intents, intermediate JSON snippets) but don’t want the noise or full token stream.
- Current streaming surfaces either stream raw tokens (too chatty) or full partial JSON frames (too heavy).
- Tool-calling semantics (tool handshake, tool commit) are intertwined with streaming and cause race conditions on flaky networks — client SDKs duplicate effort to reconcile midstream tool calls.
- Mobile/edge clients need graceful degradation modes and telemetry-friendly checkpoints.

Goals
1) Expose a first-class adapter primitive in SDKs: sample points (time or heuristic), fidelity tiers (sparse → full), and commit fences for tool invocations.
2) Allow servers to emit typed partial output (versioned small deltas) that are easy to parse and merge client-side.
3) Make tool call lifecycle explicit: PREPARE, SUGGEST, COMMIT, CANCEL, with resumability and idempotency tokens.
4) Keep bandwidth costs predictable: adapter encourages sparse sampling and aggregated deltas.
5) Provide clear telemetry hooks for latency, bytes, discarded samples, and tool-call retries.

Non-goals
- Not a replacement for full resumable session protocol (we defer heavy resume semantics to separate PRD).
- Not an LLM model architecture change — purely API/SDK and streamer surface work.

Design overview (high level)
- Sampled stream adapter (SSA) sits between the raw token stream and the SDK consumer. It receives model outputs and emits 3 families of messages: SAMPLE, DELTA, and FENCE.
  - SAMPLE: compact, human‑readable snapshot (short text + score + intent hint). Emitted periodically (time or heuristic).
  - DELTA: small typed patch (JSON Patch-ish) targeting a pre-declared schema path (e.g., summary.title). Deltas are versioned; clients can apply in-order or out-of-order if version numbers included.
  - FENCE: commit boundary for tool calls or finalization. Fence carries idempotency token and optional safe fallbacks.

Adapter policies (client-configurable)
- Sampling strategy: time-based (every N ms), token-sparse (every M tokens), intent-triggered (on confidence jump), or event-driven (on tool suggestion). SDK exposes builder to select.
- Fidelity ladder: low/med/high; server picks candidates to send per ladder; client declares maxBytesPerSecond and preferredLatency.
- Tool semantics: When SSA emits a tool SUGGEST, the client can opt to auto-accept, auto-defer, or surface for manual confirmation. SUGGEST may include a "confidence" and a "resource hint" (e.g., external API call expected).

API sketches (conceptual — SDK flavors)
- JS SDK (example usage):
  const session = StreamSession.builder()
    .withAdapter({strategy: 'token-sparse', tokens: 16, fidelity: 'med'})
    .onSample(s => ui.showProgress(s.text, s.intent))
    .onDelta(d => state.applyPatch(d.path, d.patch))
    .onFence(f => handleFence(f))
    .connect();

- REST/GRPC framing: augment existing chunk frames with header {type: "sample" | "delta" | "fence", seq: int, schema: "v1:summary"}. Payload is compact JSON or small text.

Structured output model
- Clients declare an optional tiny schema in the session init: e.g., {paths: ["summary.title","summary.bullets"], expectedTypes: ["string","array<string>"]}. Server emits DELTA patches referencing these paths. Patches are additive and idempotent via patch ids.
- Versioning: schemaVersion and patchVersion fields to allow safe roll-forward/back. Clients can ignore unknown paths.

Tool calling & handshake model
- Tool lifecycle messages embedded in SSA: TOOL_SUGGEST, TOOL_PREPARE, TOOL_COMMIT, TOOL_CANCEL. Each has tool_id and op_id.
- Commit fence: when a TOOL_COMMIT is emitted, a FENCE with commitToken is sent. Clients should ack commitToken to confirm completion; server will retry or re-route if ack not received within deadline.
- Suspend/resume: clients can request 'soft-suspend' to pause sampling while a long-running tool executes; SSA guarantees at-least-once delivery of a final DELTA with partial tool output.

SDK ergonomics & UX notes
- Minimal developer surface: the primary primitives are onSample, onDelta, onFence, and requestTool(tool_id, params). Prefer event callbacks over heavy callback chains.
- Defaults: token-sparse = 20 tokens, time-sample = 300ms; fidelity med. Sensible defaults reduce config noise.
- Mobile mode: pre-packed adapters that bias toward SAMPLE every 400ms and coalesce DELTAs into aggregated patches to save bandwidth.
- Debugging: SDK exposes a lightweight trace object per session (traceId) that lists sample timestamps, dropped samples, tool handshakes, and bytes. Trace can be uploaded to Console for problem diagnosis.

Observability & billing considerations
- Signal needs: samples_emitted, deltas_applied, fences_committed, tool_calls_initiated, tool_calls_failed, bytes_streamed, avg_sample_latency, dropped_samples.
- Billing model: keep token billing the same; introduce a small per-sample metadata meter for large DELTA payloads (>1KB) to prevent abuse.

Edge cases & failure modes
- Out-of-order patches: include seq numbers and patchVersion; SDK must be resilient (apply only when seq matches or buffer up to N).
- Network disconnects during tool commit: server should re-emit commit fence on reconnect; client can request idempotent re-apply by sending commitToken.
- Schema changes mid-session: server includes schemaVersion bump; clients must gracefully ignore unknown deltas and surface compatibility warning in trace.

Security & compliance notes
- Deltas referencing PII paths must be labeled with pii: true; SSA will not emit these to clients that do not have required ACLs in init.
- Tool suggestions that require external network access must include a resource hint and optional security classification.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should SAMPLE messages carry partial token text (cheap) or only intent/score (cheapest)? Hybrid is proposed but needs perf evaluation.
- How aggressive is server-side coalescing vs client buffering? Need experiments with mobile bandwidth.
- Billing: do we preserve pure token billing? Introduce separate meter for structured DELTA bytes?

Next steps / immediate action items
- Spike: implement JS SDK SSA prototype + small server shim to emit sample/delta/fence (ENG-1372). Owner: Marco. (2 wks)
- Simulate mobile nets with coalescing vs raw stream; measure bytes, perceived latency (user visible update time). Owner: Priya. (1 week)
- Console: small telemetry panel for sample/delta metrics (dash mock). Owner: Jonas. (2 weeks)
- Product decision meeting: finalize commit/ack semantics and billing proposal. Date: 2025-02-24.

Notes to self (brainstorm fragments)
- Consider "preview-only" sampling where samples are marked non-authoritative and never used to trigger external actions unless a fence commit arrives. Good for background UI.
- Could reuse existing session idempotency token for tool commits to avoid new token plumbing.
- Add tiny CLI tool to replay traceIds into staging for reproducing flaky tool handshakes.

TODOs
- [ ] Sketch wire format for binary streaming + sample header
- [ ] Prototype client coalescing heuristics
- [ ] Write short dev guide with examples for React Native and server-side adapters

References
- Confluence discovery notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Sampled+Stream+Adapters+Discovery
- Related ticket: ENG-1372
- Proto PR (ongoing): github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/842

End of draft.
